- **Handshake removed:** Several sources say the revision drops the `initialize`/`initialized` exchange and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header. One blog describes it as making the protocol stateless by default.
- **Per-request metadata:** Protocol version, client identity, and capabilities now go in a `_meta` object on each request. Protocol version, client info, and capabilities now travel on _meta in every request.
- **Capability discovery:** Capability queries move to a new method. One source says the server/discover method answers capability questions on demand rather than as a prerequisite.
- **Client migration:** A gateway vendor notes the revision is breaking and that clients and servers won't upgrade on the same day. Its gateway serves both generations, so legacy clients keep the handshake while new clients call statelessly.
- **Streams:** One source says broken SSE streams cannot resume. Clients issue a fresh request.
- **Caveat on status:** One source calls 2026-07-28 now the current official version, while another describes a release candidate. I couldn't confirm the final status from these results.

The main source is Cloudflare's changelog for Agents SDK v0.20.0, which adds client and server support for the MCP 2026-07-28 release candidate. Its client probes each connection with `server/discover`. If the server doesn't support the stateless protocol, the client falls back to the legacy `initialize` handshake on the same connection. Existing `addMcpServer` calls don't need a protocol-version setting. ([developers.cloudflare.com changelog](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-07-27-agents-sdk-v0.20.0-mcp-sdk-v2/))

Other points from the results:
- **Stateless servers:** `createMcpHandler` now accepts a factory that builds a new server for each request. (Cloudflare changelog)
- **McpAgent deprecated:** The release notes call McpAgent deprecated and feature-frozen, and recommend migrating to the stateless handler. ([releases.sh summary](https://releases.sh/release/rel_EvLBYcSXMjFqI7VN56Kup-mcp-2026-07-28-spec-supported-mcpagent-deprecated))
- **Protocol background:** agentgateway's docs say the 2026-07-28 revision makes MCP stateless and sessionless, keeps the older `initialize` flow working, and adds caching controls to responses such as `server/discover` and `tools/list`. ([agentgateway spec compatibility](https://agentgateway.dev/docs/standalone/latest/mcp/spec-compatibility/))

I ran one search, so I didn't check the Agents SDK's own docs or the official MCP spec text. The Cloudflare changelog is the only source describing the SDK's behavior directly.

content.text:
No, if you mean Cloudflare's Agents SDK. Since v0.20.0 (July 27, 2026), its MCP client first sends `server/discover` on each connection, which is part of the stateless MCP 2026-07-28 revision. It only falls back to the old `initialize` handshake on the same connection if the server doesn't support the new protocol. Existing `addMcpServer` calls don't need any protocol-version setting. That revision moves the protocol version, client info and capabilities into each request's `_meta`, so there's no session handshake to start with.

My only source for the SDK's behavior is Cloudflare's changelog; I didn't check its docs or the spec text. Some sources call 2026-07-28 a release candidate and others call it final. If you meant a different "Agents SDK", such as OpenAI's, I haven't checked it.
